parts.note: read as the colour of the deep, the ocean's bluish-green hue, rather than a dark shade

explanation.definitionFit: A pale bluish-green shade named after the colour of ocean water.

indicators.note: damaged tells us the letters of arches are knocked out of their order

explanation.surface: Someone is sent to look over some broken archways.
explanation.definitionFit: To inspect something closely is to go through it looking for things, a direct synonym.

parts.note: a board is a table, as in 'bed and board' or a festive board

explanation.surface: Furniture placed with cunning.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the whole clue read again: 'craftily positioned' means placed on a craft, that is, on a ship or plane. The question mark flags this pun.
explanation.definitionFit: Something on board is on a ship, plane or other vessel, so it is positioned on a craft.

clue.text: A red nose might result, it's thought

indicators.note: might result says these letters could come out in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone muses that a red nose could be the outcome, perhaps of drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: Something reasoned is logically worked out, which is to say carefully thought through.

clue.text: Girl back in the Welsh Valley she came from

indicators.note: back says the letters found are read from right to left
in says the letters sit inside the word valley

explanation.surface: A girl returns to the Welsh valley where she was born.
explanation.walkthrough: Inside VALLEY sit the letters ALLE; 'back' turns them round. 'the Welsh' and 'she came from' are surface padding.
explanation.definitionFit: A common girl's name, so an example of a girl.

parts.note: someone cross is bad-tempered or irritable

explanation.surface: Squaring up to a grumpy carpenter.
explanation.walkthrough: A joiner is a carpenter in British English; the word adds to the surface picture, hinting also at the cross that joins two lines.
explanation.definitionFit: Across from someone means facing them, so confronting is the sense of being opposite.

clue.text: Virtuous, so has head start in class

indicators.note: in says one piece goes inside the word for class

parts.note: a caste is a social class, as in the Hindu system

indicators.note: head start means the opening letter of has

explanation.surface: A good pupil gets a lead on the rest of the class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head start' takes H from 'has', which goes 'in' CASTE after its first letter; 'so' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Being pure and morally good, particularly sexually, is a sense close to virtuous.

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O

indicators.note: about says the word for talks goes round another piece

parts.note: prates means talks foolishly or at length
E stands for East, so Oriental

explanation.surface: A romance chats about Eastern purposes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts E inside PRATES to make PERATES, after the O.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine that operates works or runs, which is what something does when it functions.

clue.text: Getting very heated in a wet sort of way

definitions.text: Getting very heated in a wet sort of way

parts.words: Getting very heated in a wet sort of way
parts.note: looks like losing one's temper tearfully, but describes heat that comes from hot liquid or steam

explanation.definitionFit: Burning with hot water or steam, rather than dry heat, is the specific sense.

clue.text: A lad bore with disruption strongly like Joan Hunter Dunn

indicators.note: with disruption strongly says the letters are thrown into heavy disorder

explanation.surface: A boy carried a torch for the tennis-playing heroine of a poem.
explanation.walkthrough: Joan Hunter Dunn is the beloved tennis girl of John Betjeman's poem 'A Subaltern's Love-Song', whom the speaker adores.
explanation.definitionFit: The poem's narrator plainly finds her lovable and enchanting, so the allusion stands for that quality.

clue.text: Approached an artist-meant to obtain a picture

parts.note: came means approached, as in came near
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: Someone drew near an artist with the aim of getting a painting.
explanation.walkthrough: RA, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts, is the standard crossword artist.
explanation.definitionFit: A device whose purpose is taking photographs, so it is intended to capture an image.

parts.note: larboard is an old word for port, the left side of a ship
a ray is a beam of light

explanation.surface: Display a lamp on the ship's left side.
explanation.definitionFit: To depict or represent something is to show it, a synonym.

definitions.meaning: the surname of Sydney, the self-sacrificing lawyer in A Tale of Two Cities

explanation.surface: A container for the Dickens character from Australia's biggest city.
explanation.definitionFit: A cardboard container, and the surname of Sydney in A Tale of Two Cities.

clue.text: There's no call to stamp, the job's salaried!

definitions.meaning: a letter already prepaid needs no stamp added
read as a position, a post, that is paid

explanation.surface: A remark that nobody needs to stamp anything, since the work comes with wages.
explanation.definitionFit: With carriage prepaid so needing no stamp, and read as two words, a job that carries wages.

indicators.note: up in a down clue says the river's name is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: the Po is the river of northern Italy
posed means sat or stood still, as for a portrait

explanation.surface: Someone looked upstream and held still.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns PO into OP, as the reading goes upward in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To have been opposite or set against something is to have faced it.

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps
spite is malice or hatred

explanation.surface: Soldiers loathe any hold-up.
explanation.definitionFit: A pause or postponement, as in a respite from a sentence, is a delay.

explanation.surface: A small slope.
explanation.definitionFit: Slender in build, and to tilt or rest at an angle.

clue.text: Journalist giving heartless rogue a beer

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letters of rogue are removed, leaving its ends

parts.note: porter is a dark beer

explanation.surface: A newsman buys a crook a pint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' strips OGU from ROGUE, leaving RE; 'giving' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper writer who covers stories is a journalist.

definitions.meaning: pieces of food fried in batter

explanation.surface: Someone wastes their meals.
explanation.definitionFit: Wastes away bit by bit, and battered fried pieces of fruit or meat.

clue.text: He may well cut a fine figure

definitions.text: He may well cut a fine figure

parts.words: He may well cut a fine figure
parts.note: looks like praise for a stylish man, but describes someone who literally carves a statue

explanation.definitionFit: An artist who carves figures from stone or wood.

parts.note: reads as healthy or good features, but means the features of the head that deal with sound

explanation.definitionFit: The organs of hearing on the face are features for sound.

parts.note: march means progress, as in the march of time

explanation.surface: A Greek official gets nowhere.
explanation.definitionFit: The governor of a nome, a province of modern or ancient Greece and Egypt, was an administrator.

clue.text: Get through and support the engineer

parts.note: a pier is a supporting column of a bridge
CE is a civil engineer

explanation.surface: An engineer with a prop makes a breakthrough.
explanation.definitionFit: To pierce is to puncture or penetrate, going through something.

indicators.note: is disintegrating says the letters of Venice fall apart and re-form

explanation.surface: Venice is plainly crumbling into the lagoon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is disintegrating' rearranges VENICE; 'that's' is a link, and 'manifest' is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To evince a feeling is to display it, the verb sense of manifest.

clue.text: Academic introduction for formal royal letters

parts.note: prim means stiffly formal and proper
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A ceremonial preface for a monarch's correspondence.
explanation.definitionFit: An elementary textbook introduces learners to a subject.

indicators.note: awkwardly signals that these letters are clumsily rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone climbed clumsily under the covers.
explanation.definitionFit: To have acquired or secured something is to have got it.

parts.note: C is a musical note
ever means always, as in for ever

explanation.surface: A musical note left behind is always bright.
explanation.definitionFit: Quick-witted and bright, a direct synonym.

clue.text: See possibly about fifty as different

indicators.note: about says the scrambled word goes round another piece
possibly signals the letters of see could be rearranged

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Maybe look at around fifty as something else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' turns SEE into ESE, which goes 'about' L; 'as' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Other or besides, as in 'someone else', means different.

clue.text: Assumption which is right about a man

indicators.note: about says the word for right-wing goes round another piece

parts.note: a Tory is a political conservative, of the right
he is a male pronoun, so a man

explanation.surface: A right-winger takes something for granted about a fellow.
explanation.definitionFit: A hypothesis or supposition is an assumption.

clue.text: A metal found in fruit-metal of great value

indicators.note: found in says these pieces sit inside the word for fruit

parts.note: a plum is a fruit
tin is a metal

explanation.surface: A metal turns up in fruit; a precious metal at that.
explanation.definitionFit: A precious white metal costlier than gold.

clue.text: Less restrained, being a bit of a swine

definitions.meaning: a slice of bacon, part of a pig

explanation.surface: More reckless, and something of a pig.
explanation.definitionFit: More impetuous, and a slice of bacon cut from a pig.

indicators.note: duplicating says the word for expensive appears twice

parts.note: dear means costly

explanation.surface: Doubly costly? What a pity!
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation of dismay or sympathy, like 'oh no'.
